title: Proverbs, Chapter 17 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 17 on folios 415r, 415v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 17 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 415r, 415v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ט֤וֹב פַּ֣ת חֲ֭רֵבָה וְשַׁלְוָה־בָ֑הּ מִ֝בַּ֗יִת מָלֵ֥א זִבְחֵי־רִֽיב׃ <sup>2</sup>עֶֽבֶד־מַשְׂכִּ֗יל יִ֭מְשֹׁל בְּבֵ֣ן מֵבִ֑ישׁ וּבְת֥וֹךְ אַ֝חִ֗ים יַחֲלֹ֥ק נַחֲלָֽה׃ <sup>3</sup>מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וּבֹחֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃ <sup>4</sup>מֵ֭רַע מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־שְׂפַת־אָ֑וֶן שֶׁ֥קֶר מֵ֝זִין עַל־לְשׁ֥וֹן הַוֺּֽת׃ <sup>5</sup>לֹעֵ֣ג לָ֭רָשׁ חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ שָׂמֵ֥חַ לְ֝אֵ֗יד לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃ <sup>6</sup>עֲטֶ֣רֶת זְ֭קֵנִים בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֑ים וְתִפְאֶ֖רֶת בָּנִ֣ים אֲבוֹתָֽם׃ <sup>7</sup>לֹא־נָאוָ֣ה לְנָבָ֣ל שְׂפַת־יֶ֑תֶר אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־לְנָדִ֥יב שְׂפַת־שָֽׁקֶר׃ <sup>8</sup>אֶֽבֶן־חֵ֣ן הַ֭שֹּׁחַד בְּעֵינֵ֣י בְעָלָ֑יו אֶֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִפְנֶ֣ה יַשְׂכִּֽיל׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife. <sup>2</sup>A wise servant shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, and shall have part of the inheritance among the brethren. <sup>3</sup>The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts. <sup>4</sup>A wicked doer giveth heed to false lips; and a liar giveth ear to a naughty tongue. <sup>5</sup>Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: and he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished. <sup>6</sup>Children's children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers. <sup>7</sup>Excellent speech becometh not a fool: much less do lying lips a prince. <sup>8</sup>A gift is as a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it: whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>מְֽכַסֶּה־פֶּ֭שַׁע מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אַהֲבָ֑ה וְשֹׁנֶ֥ה בְ֝דָבָ֗ר מַפְרִ֥יד אַלּֽוּף׃ <sup>10</sup>תֵּ֣חַת גְּעָרָ֣ה בְמֵבִ֑ין מֵהַכּ֖וֹת כְּסִ֣יל מֵאָֽה׃ <sup>11</sup>אַךְ־מְרִ֥י יְבַקֶּשׁ־רָ֑ע וּמַלְאָ֥ךְ אַ֝כְזָרִ֗י יְשֻׁלַּח־בּֽוֹ׃ <sup>12</sup>פָּג֬וֹשׁ דֹּ֣ב שַׁכּ֣וּל בְּאִ֑ישׁ וְאַל־כְּ֝סִ֗יל בְּאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃ <sup>13</sup>מֵשִׁ֣יב רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה לֹא־תמיש [תָמ֥וּשׁ] רָ֝עָ֗ה מִבֵּיתֽוֹ׃ <sup>14</sup>פּ֣וֹטֵֽר מַ֭יִם רֵאשִׁ֣ית מָד֑וֹן וְלִפְנֵ֥י הִ֝תְגַּלַּ֗ע הָרִ֥יב נְטֽוֹשׁ׃ <sup>15</sup>מַצְדִּ֣יק רָ֭שָׁע וּמַרְשִׁ֣יעַ צַדִּ֑יק תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃ <sup>16</sup>לָמָּה־זֶּ֣ה מְחִ֣יר בְּיַד־כְּסִ֑יל לִקְנ֖וֹת חָכְמָ֣ה וְלֶב־אָֽיִן׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends. <sup>10</sup>A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool. <sup>11</sup>An evil man seeketh only rebellion: therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him. <sup>12</sup>Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly. <sup>13</sup>Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house. <sup>14</sup>The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with. <sup>15</sup>He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the LORD. <sup>16</sup>Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing he hath no heart to it?

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>בְּכָל־עֵ֭ת אֹהֵ֣ב הָרֵ֑עַ וְאָ֥ח לְ֝צָרָ֗ה יִוָּלֵֽד׃ <sup>18</sup>אָדָ֣ם חֲסַר־לֵ֭ב תּוֹקֵ֣עַ כָּ֑ף עֹרֵ֥ב עֲ֝רֻבָּ֗ה לִפְנֵ֥י רֵעֵֽהוּ׃ <sup>19</sup>אֹ֣הֵֽב פֶּ֭שַׁע אֹהֵ֣ב מַצָּ֑ה מַגְבִּ֥יהַּ פִּ֝תְח֗וֹ מְבַקֶּשׁ־שָֽׁבֶר׃ <sup>20</sup>עִקֶּשׁ־לֵ֭ב לֹ֣א יִמְצָא־ט֑וֹב וְנֶהְפָּ֥ךְ בִּ֝לְשׁוֹנ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃ <sup>21</sup>יֹלֵ֣ד כְּ֭סִיל לְת֣וּגָה ל֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יִ֝שְׂמַ֗ח אֲבִ֣י נָבָֽל׃ <sup>22</sup>לֵ֣ב שָׂ֭מֵחַ יֵיטִ֣ב גֵּהָ֑ה וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה תְּיַבֶּשׁ־גָּֽרֶם׃ <sup>23</sup>שֹׁ֣חַד מֵ֭חֵיק רָשָׁ֣ע יִקָּ֑ח לְ֝הַטּ֗וֹת אָרְח֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃ <sup>24</sup>אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י מֵבִ֣ין חָכְמָ֑ה וְעֵינֵ֥י כְ֝סִ֗יל בִּקְצֵה־אָֽרֶץ׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity. <sup>18</sup>A man void of understanding striketh hands, and becometh surety in the presence of his friend. <sup>19</sup>He loveth transgression that loveth strife: and he that exalteth his gate seeketh destruction. <sup>20</sup>He that hath a froward heart findeth no good: and he that hath a perverse tongue falleth into mischief. <sup>21</sup>He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy. <sup>22</sup>A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones. <sup>23</sup>A wicked man taketh a gift out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment. <sup>24</sup>Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>כַּ֣עַס לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וּ֝מֶ֗מֶר לְיוֹלַדְתּֽוֹ׃ <sup>26</sup>גַּ֤ם עֲנ֣וֹשׁ לַצַּדִּ֣יק לֹּא־ט֑וֹב לְהַכּ֖וֹת נְדִיבִ֣ים עַל־יֹֽשֶׁר׃ <sup>27</sup>חוֹשֵׂ֣ךְ אֲ֭מָרָיו יוֹדֵ֣עַ דָּ֑עַת וקר־ [יְקַר־] ר֝֗וּחַ אִ֣ישׁ תְּבוּנָֽה׃ <sup>28</sup>גַּ֤ם אֱוִ֣יל מַ֭חֲרִישׁ חָכָ֣ם יֵחָשֵׁ֑ב אֹטֵ֖ם שְׂפָתָ֣יו נָבֽוֹן׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him. <sup>26</sup>Also to punish the just is not good, nor to strike princes for equity. <sup>27</sup>He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit. <sup>28</sup>Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.
